title: Sushi

constraints.text: N ≤ 300 dishes, each with 1, 2 or 3 pieces

explanation: Which dish has which count doesn't matter — only how many dishes have 1, 2 or 3 pieces. Solve the self-loop (empty dish chosen) algebraically.
traps: The state can stay the same when an empty dish is picked; solve for E instead of recursing forever.

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[c1][c2][c3] = expected remaining operations with c1, c2, c3 dishes having 1, 2, 3 pieces
dp[mask] = expected operations given which dishes are empty
options.why: 2^300; dishes with the same count are interchangeable.

options.text: dp[k] = expected operations with k pieces left in total
options.why: Different distributions of the same total behave differently.

options.text: dp[i] = probability that all sushi is gone after i operations
options.why: Unbounded number of steps; you want an expectation.

extraLayers.explanation: By symmetry only the counts per piece-number matter: 301³ / 6 states.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.why: Ignores the chance of picking an empty dish (the self-loop).

options.text: dp = N / (c1 + c2 + c3) + dp with one piece fewer
options.why: Right first term, but the next state depends on which kind of dish was hit.

extraLayers.explanation: Write E = 1 + (c0/N)·E + Σ (c_k/N)·E', then solve for E. Iterate c3, then c2, then c1 in increasing order.
